items.title: Brazil has made gains against Amazon deforestation, but lasting protection is a challenge
items.summary: Recent drops in Brazil's deforestation have been celebrated as a historic achievement. Forest loss in the Amazon fell by 23.5% in 2025 compared with the previous year. This drop contributed to a 21% national reduction in overall clear-cutting—the lowest level recorded since 2016.

items.title: This new concrete is stronger and pulls CO2 from the air
items.summary: Researchers have created a concrete mixture that is both stronger and capable of absorbing carbon dioxide. items.title: Water-based process separates zirconium and hafnium with fivefold higher efficiency
items.summary: Oregon State University scientists have patented a better, more environmentally friendly process for separating two metals that are critical in their pure forms for the semiconductor and atomic energy industries.

items.title: More social media use linked to poorer sleep and self-rated health among college students
items.summary: College students who spend more time on social media tend to sleep worse, and that may have consequences for how they perceive their own health, according to a new George Mason University study.

items.title: New study finds personality is key in hiring effective leaders
items.summary: A new study from Michigan State University found that the personality characteristics that get you promoted to a leadership role aren't necessarily the qualities that make you a good leader.

items.title: A strange circle on satellite maps turned out to be a 390-million-year-old impact crater
items.summary: An amateur astronomer searching satellite maps for a Quebec camping spot accidentally discovered a massive ancient impact crater. Scientists later found shatter cones that confirmed the 25-kilometer-wide structure was blasted into Earth roughly 390 million years ago.

items.title: El Niño weather pattern enters record territory: Scientist
items.summary: The strengthening El Niño weather pattern has tied for the most intense on record on a widely used metric, a senior scientist told AFP on Monday, even as its influence is already being felt from Central America to Indonesia.
